system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s assertions that terms are “market”, agreed or “FINAL” are not evidence of Buyer approval. Recommendations below reflect the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition; the underlying SPA and DD records have not been supplied for verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and fraud claims. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recourse arrangements; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible** basket, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for separately protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated; the proposed structure leaves Buyer bearing significant cumulative loss. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least two full reporting cycles, with timely notified claims surviving expiry and longer periods for other categories. | **Seek 24–36 months for general warranties and reject blanket application**; latent issues may not emerge within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties, without basket/de minimis, capped at least at the purchase price and surviving materially longer. | **Seek AUD 24m cap and six-year contractual notification period**, preserving longer applicable rights; defective title or capacity jeopardises the entire investment. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is stated. | Express preservation of fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment claims, including relevant attribution to Seller, plus non-excludable rights. | **Carve these claims out of caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure/knowledge bars and remedy restrictions**; Seller must not obtain contractual protection for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the relevant matter; a fixed, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific, warranty-linked disclosures and an archived record**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable through diligence or public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; preferably no knowledge exclusion at all. | **Delete; if unavoidable, restrict to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, with Seller proving it**; discoverability is not informed acceptance of risk. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, although final consent and satisfaction of conditions are absent. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions without unacceptable changes. | **Require evidence of effective, satisfactory consent before Completion, with a long-stop termination right**; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, discharge of debt and release of all relevant securities and guarantees at Completion. | **Pay the lender directly from Seller proceeds against binding payoff/release arrangements, with registration evidence to follow promptly**; Buyer should not inherit debt or unsecured reliance on a later release. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unresolved. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable on-costs, through payment or an express price deduction. | **Quantify entitlements and on-costs and include them expressly in funds flow, with no double counting**; omission could shift Seller’s transaction costs onto Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified and assignment evidence is absent. | Verified payment status, effective ownership/assignment of relevant IP and protection for resulting title, use and third-party claims. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment before Completion, backed by a broader specific indemnity and appropriate retention**; paying an invoice alone may not resolve the IP ownership exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, allegedly immaterial matter; access, scope, notification requirements and loss remain unknown. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal notification assessment and protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation milestones and a specific indemnity for resulting liabilities and reasonable response costs, supported by retention if unresolved**; uncertainty neither proves a breach nor justifies dismissing the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals are ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess all **AUD 330,000** together for timing, scope, commitment, termination rights and accounting treatment. | **Verify the contracts before allocating cost; seek consent controls and adjustment only where justified**; neither ordinary-course treatment nor a debt-like deduction follows automatically from the disclosures. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Broad limitations and exclusive-remedy provisions apply to all Claims unless excluded. | Express, coordinated regimes for general, fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, covenant and price-adjustment claims, with fraud separately preserved. | **Rewrite the application provisions and precedence rules across clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5**; otherwise blanket wording may defeat negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding 100%. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options and other rights, plus valid transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, certificates, searches and supporting instruments; require title warranties and releases**; the register is evidence, not a complete title investigation. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled within the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with suitable statutory-tail protection; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties with risk-appropriate survival and caps. | **Keep both expressly open pending specialist diligence and agreed drafting**; generic limits are not a substitute for allocating historic tax and core-IP risks. |

**Disclosure discipline:** Do not turn the office lease’s notification obligation into a consent requirement, or Mossvale’s assignment restriction into a share-sale consent requirement, without supporting contractual wording. Disclosed facts should inform targeted protections—not be treated as either proven breaches or accepted Buyer risks.
=== END ADVICE ===
